metadata.title: Open problems from the Length Optimization event at MDS 2026
metadata.abstract: During the Minisymposium on Length Optimization as part of the International Conference "Mathematics Days in Sofia - 2026", the participants collected the following open problems: 1. Find any non-trivial upper and lower bounds for the degree of a branching point in the Gilbert-Steiner problem with cost-function $c(x) = x^p$ in the metric space $X = \mathbb{R}^d$ for large $d$ and fixed $p > 1/2$ (see Section 1). 2. Determine whether a typical trajectory of a given branched optimal traffic plan has bounded length. To find the optimal transport plan between the Dirac measure in the center of a circle and the Lebesgue measure on the circle (see Section 2). 3. To find the maximal distance minimizers for any explicit compact sets (see Section 3). 4. What is the minimal $C$ such that for any set of $n$ points in the three-dimensional unit cube, there is a tour through all these $n$ points with the sum of the cubes of its edge lengths at most $C$ (see Section 4). 5. To explore parallels between tropical caustics and Steiner trees: do caustics really need convexity (see Section 5).
metadata.comment: 12 pages, 8 figures. Open problems from the Length Optimization minisymposium, Mathematics Days in Sofia 2026 (6-7 July 2026). Problems by D. Cherkashin, A. Prouff, Y. Teplitskaya, A. Gordeev, M. Shkolnikov

analysis.progressType: 长度最优化开放问题汇集
analysis.workSummary: 汇集MDS2026长度最优化讨论中的问题：高维Gilbert–Steiner分支度界、branched traffic典型路径长度与圆周输运、显式最大距离最小化子、三维点集巡回边长立方和的最优常数，以及tropical caustics与Steiner树及凸性的关系。
analysis.breakthrough: 提供可选研究题与跨方向联系，成果性质是问题清单。
analysis.limitations: 所列核心题目为开放问题，不是新定理或解答；p>1/2、高维及三维立方泛函等参数范围应保留。 当前数学解读依据摘要，尚未逐步审读证明。
